response.coreIdea: Dot products of wider random vectors spread out like √d_k, so attention divides them by √d_k to keep the softmax soft.
response.title: Why attention divides by √d_k
response.dek: A dot product of two d_k-wide random vectors has a spread of about √d_k. Divide by √d_k and the softmax stays soft at any width.

sections.heading: Scores from dot products
paragraphs: Each query is compared with every key by a dot product, `q·k`. A softmax turns those scores into weights that add up to 1.

figures.title: Scaling keeps attention soft
figures.caption: Attention weights over eight keys for one random query. Drag d_k, then divide by √d_k.
figures.alt: Bar chart of attention weights over eight keys at width 4, fairly even. As d_k grows without scaling, one bar takes almost all the weight; with scaling the bars stay spread.

figures.title: Spread grows like √d_k
figures.caption: The standard deviation of a dot product of two random d_k-wide vectors.
figures.alt: Line chart of score spread against key width from 1 to 512, rising like a square root: 2 at width 4, 8 at width 64, about 22.6 at width 512.
